reviews.review:
[h2]Campaign & co-op[/h2]
++++ co-op campaigns are a rare treat. More of that! Quadruple thumbs up
++ the voice acting is great comedy. I was in constant suspense whether or not the conversations could get even more "manly"
+++ the atmosphere is as thick as can be – fighting everywhere, imperial soldiers dying in the distance, mega cities in ruins. Very lead-heavy atmosphere so to say.
+++ I’ve seen too many dark dungeons and corridors. this game feels spacious and really lets me absorb the vibe of different planets. Extra points for borrowing from Elden Ring
-- as usual, the campaign is a bit too short. for the price of this game you could probably get more co-op fun. like e.g. rock climbing. yeah, haven't done that in a while
-- the ops missions and rewards might’ve needed to be more “roguelike” for a motivating end game loop. But who cares, I enjoyed the campaign and will find myself a new lover now
-- remind yourself to set ops to private mode, unless you want ToughMarine93 to join your squad, pick the same class, and prevent the mission from starting
-- would’ve loved to just get back to the main menu in case of a disconnect. But you’ll get to see the glorious insides of your battle barge multiple times trying to reconnect
-- Lore, audio logs, and story dialogues were lost on me. when a thousand zerglings come rushing at me, I’m unable to pay attention. Maybe I’m just too old now

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
++ from 0 to 100 kills in 10 seconds
++ “hard” is actually challenging. I was burning through my stim packs so quickly I got addicted
++ AI comrade is as stupid as he sounds but never fails to reanimate me with a caring bro caress
-- the jet pack missions were fun, but the jet packs in operations mode seem to have a cough
-- play style never really feels agile. though it really gets across that you're a metric ton of a man
-- once you’re surrounded by enemies, you’ll probably forget about your heavy weapon and slice enemies in melee. I mostly sticked to one of the very similar mid-range rifles which let me keep my distance
-- are finishing moves more satisfying with an extra button? I play souls likes with a gamepad, but with this game I had to use mouse & keyboard

[h2]Other[/h2]
-- there's a series of fun little puzzle games they use in place of menus. or maybe they're supposed to be menus? who knows! I prefer a UI with a focus on usability
-- whatever the idea behind the unlockable armor pieces is, the clunky customization won't let you be as creative as with tabletop figurines. next time maybe just include an armor paint shop so I can wear the colors of my glorious Bursting Veins Marines which I just made up

can't say anything bad about the performance. I have a Ryzen 3900x + RTX 4070
amazing I love ripping the balls off the demons

The story despite being short doesnt waste any of your time, each level is visually a masterpiece and the action gameplay is action packed. If it were just the story I would still recommend this but this game also has PVE and PVP game modes complete with customisation and PVE skill trees.

This game has the most satisfying combat mechanics i've ever seen. I have put hundreds of hours over xbox and pc and have maxed out all classes and I still feel like im making progress. Whether you are a loyalists or a heretic you'll love this game. 40K/10 the emperor protects
